title: Unique points of base-change fibres
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $k\to k\prime$ be a field extension, and let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a separated, locally finite type, quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $\dim |C|\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Put $C_{k\prime}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\prime$ and let $\pi:C_{k\prime}\to C$ be the projection [def-pc-base-change]. For every $c\in|C|$, there exists exactly one $z\in|C_{k\prime}|$ with $\pi(z)=c$.

proof.text: Apply zeroDimensional_baseChange_geometry and retain its pointwise residue-field isomorphism conclusion. No second use of Nullstellensatz or explicit identification with k is needed.

For each pullback triplet T, the left map in its residue-field pushout is an isomorphism, since it is a residue-field congruence followed by the structure residue-field map. Its Spec map is an isomorphism. The pullback square isPullback_SpecMap_tensor therefore makes Spec.map T.tensorInr an isomorphism (IsPullback.isIso_snd_of_isIso). Its underlying homeomorphism injects Spec T.tensor into the singleton spectrum of the field at T.y, giving Subsingleton (Spec T.tensor).

For any c, exists_preimage_pullback with the unique point of Spec k-prime gives a point above c, since Spec k is a singleton. If two points lie above c, their ofPoint triplets agree by Triplet.ext: their first coordinates agree by hypothesis and their second coordinates agree because Spec k-prime is a singleton. carrierEquiv_eq_iff and the singleton tensor spectrum identify their carrierEquiv images; injectivity of carrierEquiv identifies the points.
